note: Process and structural evals. No comparative A/B panel has been run; EVALS.md records that absence and names the three tasks that would close it.

cases.prompt: Build a digest email from these 30 items.
assert: All 30 items appear in the output.
No item is dropped, truncated away, or moved to a 'see the rest on the web' stub in place of being rendered.
The run does not suggest reducing the item count as a fix.
cases.why: The intuitive fix is fewer items and the evidence goes the other way. This is the single most likely regression.

cases.prompt: Build a digest email from these 24 items.
assert: Between 2 and 4 items carry the featured treatment.
Between 5 and 9 carry the compact treatment.
Every remaining item is title-only.
Each item block carries a machine-readable tier marker.
cases.why: Kong et al. localises the measured benefit to selective prominence. Without the marker every tier rule passes vacuously.

cases.prompt: Add a table of contents to the top of this digest so readers can jump to a section.
assert: The output contains no href starting with '#'.
The run states why, naming iOS client failure or the tracking gap.
A summary block is still produced, with links pointing outward to destinations.
cases.why: A direct request for the thing the evidence forbids. The skill should serve the intent and refuse the mechanism.

cases.prompt: This email is mostly images. Check it will not land in spam.
assert: The run does not assert a 60/40 or 80/20 text-to-image ratio requirement.
It checks instead that content survives with images stripped.
If the ratio is mentioned, it is named as untraceable rather than applied.
cases.why: Three of four research backends rejected the ratio rule; one proposed gating on it. The rejected version must not resurface.

cases.prompt: Use our logo, it is at assets/brand/mark.svg.
assert: The output contains no <svg> element.
The logo is rasterised to PNG before use, or the run says it must be.
The reason names Gmail stripping the tag.
cases.why: Silent failure: the mark disappears in Gmail and nothing reports an error.

assert: Exit code is 1.
At least 10 distinct rules report an error.
Each error names the class of evidence behind it.
cases.why: A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Verified at 13 errors.

cases.prompt: Render the 24-item fixture and gate it.
assert: Exit code is 0.
HTML is under 90KB.
The report states that passing gates is not the same as the email being worth reading.
cases.why: The honest-baseline case. Verified at 0 errors, 24.7KB.

cases.prompt: Is this layout better than a flat list?
assert: The answer states that no published study compares the two.
It does not claim the tiered layout is measured to be better.
It names a test that would settle it, measured on clicks rather than opens.
cases.why: The central claim is an inference. A skill that dresses it as measurement is overclaiming from its own corpus.
